trust_decision.summary: Whether an LLM-supplied run_shell command string may be launched as a process; decided only by _is_cli_command_allowed, which checks the first shlex token against an app allow-list (which includes explorer) plus a regex denylist, and accepts any trailing arguments.

landing_point.why: The summary names run_shell and explorer.exe; the allow-list entries for explorer are the first thing an engineer would look at.

fix_sites.entry_point: MCP tool run_shell (CommandLineExecutor, HostAgent/AppAgent action server)
fix_sites.module_kind: allow-list constant in MCP local server
validator function (token-count check: exactly one token)
prompt data (removes the 'powerpnt <file>' example at line 239 and the 'explorer' example at line 263)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue that the report is about explorer.exe only, so arguments to the other allow-listed launchers (msedge/chrome/code/winword switches, file paths) are legitimate 'open a file' use, which the shipped prompt example even demonstrates (ufo/prompts/examples/visual/host_agent_example.yaml:239).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A bare allow-listed app name, including surrounding whitespace, quotes and mixed case (e.g. '  "NoTePaD.ExE"  '), must still launch via Popen([name], shell=False); an over-broad fix that rejects quotes or case-folds the argv breaks it (fix.diff:137-142).

O6_input_shapes: explorer with a file path, UNC path, shell: URI or URL argument (fix.diff:52-55)
other allow-listed apps with switches: code --install-extension, msedge --gpu-launcher=, chrome --utility-cmd-prefix=, winword /m (fix.diff:62-65)
allow-listed app with a file or URL argument, including an empty quoted argument (fix.diff:66-71)
unbalanced quote / quoted absolute path to an allow-listed binary (fix.diff:83-87)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: execute_command takes a separate args list; a planted app-launch variant that validates only `command` while appending args would mirror the flaw.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already treats command and args separately (ufo/automator/app_apis/shell/shell_client.py:486-490), so a maintainer could plausibly check only the command name.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Session launches Popen([app_name, file]) with a file argument from the plan reader; a copy that takes app_name or file from LLM output would be an argument-injection sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The 'launch app with file' pattern already exists here, and it is the legitimate behaviour the fix removed from run_shell.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: os.startfile on an LLM-supplied path, guarded by a .pdf suffix check in another function (ufo/client/mcp/local_servers/pdf_reader_mcp_server.py:204); a variant without the suffix gate would be a launcher-via-file-association sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Opening a document 'like a human' with the default handler is an existing feature, and the suffix check is separated from the startfile call.

O9_family: argument injection / incomplete allow-list on a process launcher (CWE-88, CWE-184)

O10_build.project_tests: None for cli_mcp_server at the pinned commit. The fix adds tests/test_cli_mcp_server_security.py, which mocks subprocess.Popen and time.sleep, so it can run on Linux. The module calls ufo.config.get_config at import time (ufo/client/mcp/local_servers/cli_mcp_server.py:22-27).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Remove explorer/explorer.exe from ALLOWED_CLI_COMMANDS (or add a path/URL regex) and leave arguments to msedge/chrome/code/winword allowed.

out_of_scope_notes: ufo/automator/app_apis/shell/shell_client.py:347-437 has a separate PowerShell run_shell with its own allow-list and denylist; it is a different sink and a different protection.
ufo/prompts/examples/nonvisual/host_agent_example.yaml:327-344 and ufo/prompts/share/base/host_agent.yaml:26 still suggest launching explorer; these are prompt text, not code routes.
unverified: Other Windows app-launch tools were checked only by grep for Popen/startfile/ShellExecute/Application.start; a pywinauto-based launcher under another name could have been missed.
The advisory text itself was not available; the summary comes from the candidate record and the fix commit message.
